Its number of active attention heads determines the effective widths of the embeddings, attention projections, feed-forward layers, and the output head, forming a nested family of subnetworks within a single parameter set. We introduce a static-to-elastic conversion pipeline that, starting from a pre-trained model checkpoint, includes importance-driven weight reordering and stochastic subnetwork training with knowledge distillation. We extend this principle to multimodal inference through an elastic projection module whose output width follows the active text width. HydraLLM covers a wider range of active parameter configurations than FFN-only elastic architectures. With 75% of heads active, HydraLLM achieves 2.2 percentage points higher TriviaQA accuracy than a state-of-the-art nested baseline configuration which has 17.25% more parameters. With 50% of heads active, our multimodal model achieves a CLIPScore comparable to that of the 7$\times$ larger Gemma 3 4B model. With only 25% of heads active, HydraLLM increases token-generation throughput by 75.3% over the full-width configuration.

papers.title: A low-dimensional dynamical basis for tongue shape control
papers.abstract: Speech production involves the control of a high-dimensional articulatory system with many degrees-of-freedom, but a widespread hypothesis is that speakers navigate this complexity using a set of lower-dimensional control variables. Common candidates for these control variables include individual articulators (e.g. tongue body) and abstract tract variables (e.g. tongue body constriction location), but identifying the most appropriate coordinate system for articulatory control remains an open question. In this study, we advance a model in which holistic tongue shape modes represent a potential low-dimensional control basis for a simple dynamical law. We first discover empirical tongue shape modes in a cross-speaker coordinate space and then fit the model to ultrasound data on monophthongal vowels from 36 speakers of British English. A three-dimensional linear point attractor fitted to these time-varying modes recovers the dynamics of tongue shape with a high degree of accuracy. This suggests that complex tongue movement can arise from independent modes that linearly combine under simple dynamical laws, thereby relocating some complexity from the control signal to the coordinate system. We show that this framing explains why one-dimensional articulatory measures can exhibit observable nonlinearities, and hypothesize that shape modes are a plausible kinematic expression of underlying muscle synergies.

papers.title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
papers.abstract: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.

papers.title: Are Single-Leader-Multi-Follower Problems Particular Cases of Bilevel Optimization?
papers.abstract: For more than 20 years, single-leader multi-follower (SLMF) problems have been treated as a more difficult class of problems in comparison to bilevel optimization. In this work we challenge this common belief, studying whether SLMF problems can be reformulated as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. We consider both optimistic and pessimistic formulations. For the optimistic case the answer is positive: We derive an equivalent bilevel problem by representing the followers' equilibria as fixed points of the solution mapping of a single optimization problem. For pessimistic problems, the situation is different. We show that every optimistic trilevel problem admits an equivalent pessimistic SLMF formulation with two followers. Conversely, for every pessimistic SLMF problem verifying a mild attainability assumption we establish an equivalent optimistic trilevel reformulation. The reformulations are easy, readily tractable, and they preserve convex and linear data. Thus, unless $\text{NP}=Σ_2^p$, we deduce as byproduct that multiple followers induce an unexpected complexity gap between optimistic and pessimistic approaches, which is not the case when considering one follower alone.

papers.title: On MRD constacyclic codes over inseparable field extensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct MRD constacyclic codes of length $p$ over an inseparable field extension $L/K$, where $K$ has characteristic $p$. In particular, these codes cannot be obtained from known constructions.

papers.title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation
papers.abstract: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) offers a unique opportunity to map the QCD phase diagram in the high-baryon-density region. In particular, higher-order cumulants ($C_r$) of event-by-event proton number distributions have been proposed as sensitive probes of the nuclear-matter phase structure. In this work, $^{\text{238}}$U+$^{\text{238}}$U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV are generated using the JAM2 model and then processed through the CEE fast simulation with detector responses. Experimental analysis procedures, including centrality determination and particle identification, are also implemented. Proton-number cumulants up to fourth order and their ratios are calculated and compared with the true values. A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. An additional factor is also included to account for acceptance losses caused by the azimuthal gap between the two TPCs. Within the uncertainties of the current data sample, the corrected cumulants and cumulant ratios are consistent with their generator-level values. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. These results provide a simulation-based assessment of the analysis feasibility and statistical requirements for proton-number fluctuation measurements at CEE.

papers.title: Deterministic Global Minimum Cut Using $\tilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ Cut Queries
papers.abstract: Finding a global minimum cut in an unweighted graph is a fundamental task in the cut-query model. While there exists a randomized algorithm for this task using $\tilde O(n)$ queries, known deterministic algorithms use $\tilde{O}(n^{5/3})$ queries. We improve upon this result and give a simple deterministic algorithm that finds a global minimum cut using $\tilde O(\min\left\{ nδ,n^2/δ\right\})$ cut queries, which equals $\tilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ in the worst case, where $δ$ is the minimum degree of the graph. The key ingredient in our approach is an efficient maximum $s,t$-flow algorithm, for the case when the minimum $s,t$-cut has value at most $δ$.

papers.title: A Smaller Subspace is All You Need: Efficient ISAC Beamforming via Dimensionality Reduction
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a critical technology for the sixth generation (6G) wireless networks. Under monostatic sensing mode, achieving a balance between communication and sensing performance via optimal beamforming is a critical research problem. In multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems, such beamforming problems are of substantial computational complexity due to the large number of antennas. Existing methods exploit exact subspaces of lower dimensions to speed up the beamforming process where the complexity is proportional to the number of communication users and sensing targets instead of antennas. In this paper, it is demonstrated that the beamforming problem can be solved in an even lower-dimensional subspace with only a small sensing performance loss. Numerical results compare the sensing performance and computational complexity of ISAC beamforming problem in the exact subspace and smaller subspaces.

papers.title: Model Checking for Noisy Toric Words
papers.abstract: Toric words have recently gained attention as a means to model the behaviour of dynamical systems such as linear loops. This work is concerned with describing when the toric model is precise enough to decide whether the trace of a system is contained in an omega-regular language. Our contributions are threefold. (i) We use topological means to generalise a class of toric words by defining noise-robust dynamical systems and their sets of noisy traces. We prove that all noisy traces of a system are almost-periodic, and have the same set of recurrent factors. (ii) We apply the abstract techniques above to concrete sequences obtained as sign descriptions of real algebraic linear recurrence sequences (LRS), and show that the language-membership problem for sign descriptions of LRS with few dominant roots is decidable. (iii) We show that noisy traces of noise-robust dynamical systems are indistinguishable to a prefix-independent omega-regular language, and inclusion is decidable provided the common language of their recurrent factors is recursive. We incidentally obtain properties of prefix-independent omega-regular languages that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Pricing and Operation for Hybrid Electric and Hydrogen Vehicle Stations
papers.abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen fuel cell vehi- cles (HFCVs) are promising technologies in the efforts to reduce carbon emissions. Challenges such as limited infrastructure, con- sumer dissatisfaction, and electrical grid strain inhibit progress in the adoption of these technologies. A zero emission vehicle (ZEV) station, capable of handling EVs and HFCVs, addresses these challenges by focusing on maximizing station profit and consumer utility, while minimizing grid impacts. The purpose of this research is to develop a realistic simulation of a ZEV station that is capable of handling real-time pricing decisions enabled by reinforcement learning (RL) and to compare the performance of the RL agent to static pricing methods. After training, the RL agent gains 10.83% greater station profit than the baseline manual parameter search. This work serves as a useful tool for ZEV station owners when handling complex pricing and purchasing decisions.

papers.title: S-GAP: Stealthy Graph Attack Primitives for Graph Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Graph Large Language Models (GraphLLMs) enable powerful semantic understanding and reasoning over Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs), while their semantic reasoning may exhibit vulnerabilities to perturbations in node text and graph structure under adversarial attack evaluation. Existing attacks typically construct textual and structural perturbations in separate stages guided by distinct realization intents. However, this separation results in attack-intent fragmentation, causing semantic incoherence between the two perturbation types, thereby undermining attack stealth and making them easier for GraphLLMs to identify and disregard, ultimately weakening attack effectiveness. To avoid attack-intent fragmentation, we propose the Graph Attack Primitive (GAP), an atomic semantic representation that unifies textual and structural perturbations under a coherent attack intent. By carefully calibrating the semantic composition of a GAP, we can achieve strong attack effectiveness while maintaining sufficient attack stealth. Furthermore, we introduce S-GAP (Stealthy GAP), a multi-agent framework that iteratively refines the semantic content of the GAP. The framework unifies GAP planning and realization and continuously refines this process through surrogate evaluation and textual feedback. Extensive experiments across four datasets, three GraphLLMs, and two attack settings show that S-GAP improves ASR over the strongest baselines by 7.02% on average while producing more relationally plausible perturbations, exposing critical vulnerabilities in current GraphLLMs and motivating more robust defenses.

papers.title: Graphlet-based Decentralized Finance Transaction Method Classification
papers.abstract: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) transactions involve complex interactions among accounts, smart contracts, and tokens. We investigate whether network topology can identify transaction methods that describe DeFi operations. We extract directed graphlet features to classify the 30 most frequent methods. Our results show that graphlet features complement event log counts in improving classification performance. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we further derive model explanations that reveal method-specific graphlet structural patterns.

papers.title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line
papers.abstract: We prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which are simple or lie on the critical line, is greater than $8/9$, with zeros counted with multiplicity.

papers.title: Multiplayer games on regular graphs under aspiration-driven imitation: Fixation probabilities and the dilution principle
papers.abstract: We investigate how cooperation evolves in multiplayer games on regular graphs of degree $k$ when individuals base their decisions on both their own aspiration levels and the success of their neighbors. We calculate explicit first-order formulas for fixation probabilities using pair approximation and diffusion methods under weak selection. These formulas separate aspiration effects from payoff effects filtered by the graph. We show that increasing the graph degree attenuates the selection effects driven by payoffs. In contrast, the contribution of the aspiration gap $Δα=α_D-α_C$ is independent of graph degree at first order. We apply the framework to public goods, stag-hunt, and snowdrift games and obtain corresponding conditions for the evolutionary success of cooperation. In the public goods and stag-hunt games, the conditions at large degree retain cost terms, so cooperation requires a sufficiently positive aspiration gap to compensate for the cost of contributing. In the snowdrift game, both benefit and cost contributions vanish in the locally tree-like regime at large degree, leaving the aspiration gap as the leading first-order contribution. Monte Carlo simulations on connected random regular graphs of degree $k$ are consistent with the first-order predictions within their formal regime of validity, while simulations outside this regime are interpreted only as qualitative checks of the predicted trends.

papers.title: When Evidence Vanishes: Distilling Visual-Evidence Dependency in Medical Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Compact medical vision-language models (VLMs) can answer clinical questions correctly without reliably using the image, relying instead on question wording or learned priors. Standard knowledge distillation copies a teacher's answer preference on the original image, but it leaves unchecked whether that preference is conditional on the visual evidence required by the question. We study this missing target as medical visual evidence dependency: support for the correct answer should decrease when the matched evidence is absent. We introduce Evidence-Conditioned Dependency Distillation (ECDD), which pairs each training image with a control matched to the evidence level and distills the teacher's drop in answer margin across the pair. A lower bound objective transfers positive dependency by penalizing only shortfalls, while original-image supervision preserves task accuracy. The same formulation applies when the evidence is a queried clinical region, a surgical instrument, or whole-image visual content. Across three medical VQA settings, ECDD keeps original-image accuracy competitive with distillation and alignment baselines while making answer support more sensitive to evidence removal. Under the DME headline objective, for example, the positive-case margin response to target rather than random masking rises from 0.786 with KD to 2.023 with ECDD, while original-image accuracy differs by 0.11 points. These results suggest that medical VLM distillation should transfer both the teacher's answer preference and its dependence on visual evidence.

papers.title: QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
papers.abstract: Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents. We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not. In high-stakes decisions, e.g., which company to acquire or which customer to target, comparing diverse, well-reasoned options can be more useful than a single ranked list. We formalize open-ended recommendation as building a diverse, high-quality set of recommendations, each an item together with a hypothesis, a natural-language reason why the item fits the needs of a decision maker. We propose QD-Rec, a quality--diversity method that selects items with a contextual bandit and generates hypotheses with a foundation model from earlier ones kept in an archive as stepping stones. A new recommendation enters the archive if it is novel or better than its nearest neighbor. Across M&A, customer targeting, and paper and book recommendation, QD-Rec gives the highest mean quality and builds the largest archive in most settings.

papers.title: On decomposition thresholds for odd cycles
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotic minimum-degree threshold for decompositions into cycles of a fixed odd length. We prove that, for each odd integer $\ell\ge3$, every $\eps>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $C_\ell$-divisible graph $G$ with minimum degree $δ(G)\ge (\ell/(2\ell-2)+\eps)n$ has a $C_\ell$-decomposition, where $C_{\ell}$ denotes the cycle of length $\ell$. This settles the remaining cases $\ell=5,7,\ldots,71$ and completes the determination of the thresholds for all odd cycles. Our main ingredient is a sharp fractional decomposition theorem for weighted triangles: for every real $a\ge 1$,every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $δ(G)\ge \left(\frac12+\frac{1}{2(a+1)}\right)n$ admits a fractional decomposition into triangles with edge weights $a,1,1$.

papers.title: Single-electron fluorine bonding. II. Benchmarking Minnesota density functional approximations and popular ab initio methods for binding energies (BEs) and F-bond distances
papers.abstract: Companion paper I (Khanal and Arunan, in this issue; arXiv:2610.16629 [physics.chem-ph]) reported reference BEs and F-bond distances for two new databases SEFB-15 (DF$\cdots$CH$_3$) and CSFB-14 (DF$\cdots$NH$_3$). Here, we assess performance of popular ab initio methods (MP2, MP3, MP4(DQ), MP4(SDQ), CCSD, and QCISD) with valence- and full-electron correlation treatments, and sixteen Minnesota DFAs, including M06-2X already assessed in companion paper I. CCSD/AVDZ reproduces reference F-bond distances closely, although BEs predicted by it deviate more. Among the 16 Minnesota DFAs, M08-HX reliably reproduces both reference values for DF$\cdots$CH$_3$ and DF$\cdots$NH$_3$, comparable to M05-2X and M06-2X for DF$\cdots$NH$_3$. Selected meta-GGAs (M06-L, M11-L, and MN15-L) exhibit spurious fractional charge transfer in cationic complexes even at infinite separation, whereas hybrid Minnesota DFAs do not, except M05 and M06 for NH$_3$F$^+\cdots$CH$_3$ and NH$_2$F$_2^+\cdots$CH$_3$. Although M08-HX shows slightly larger monomer delocalization error than M05-2X and M06-2X, it is more reliable for predicting BEs of SEFB complexes, indicating that monomer delocalization error alone does not govern DFA performance. Bader's intermolecular delocalization indices (DIs) further support M08-HX as more reliable than M05-2X and M06-2X for SEFB, while the larger DIs from M05-2X and M06-2X explain the degraded performance of their dispersion-corrected variants for DF$\cdots$CH$_3$, with only a minor impact for DF$\cdots$NH$_3$, highlighting the system-dependent nature of functional delocalization error. Present work reveals that M08-HX is more reliable than M05-2X and M06-2X for open-shell DF$\cdots$CH$_3$ complexes, while all three functionals show comparable reliability for closed-shell DF$\cdots$NH$_3$ complexes.

papers.title: Magnetic Field-assisted Crystallographic Selection During Grain Growth in Non-Magnetic Polycrystals: A Phase-Field Study
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields drive grain boundary migration in non-magnetic systems through anisotropic susceptibility, yet how the local orientation can affect the resulting collective grain growth behavior remains unclear. We employ a phase-field model to investigate magnetic-field-assisted grain growth in the diamagnetic Bi. This study provides a mechanistic basis for using static and dynamically varied magnetic fields to control texture development and grain growth kinetics in weakly magnetic materials. We also identify the conditions under which magnetic-field-driven orientation selection produces a distinct bimodal grain-size distribution. The bicrystal studies establish that boundary migration is governed by the magnetic free-energy difference between differently oriented grains, while polycrystalline field-sweep simulations reveal a transition from capillary-dominated coarsening to magnetically biased texture selection. For unbiased orientation distributions, magnetic selection remains distributed; however, when a small population of grains is strongly favored, the driving force localizes and exhibits bimodal coarsening characterized by enlarged favored grains embedded within a fine-grained matrix, even without grain boundary energy anisotropy, particle pinning, or heterogeneity. The field removal and field reorientation simulations further show that magnetic field history can redirect the coarsening pathway.

papers.title: Neutrino Anomalies and Tensions: Experimental Status and Theoretical Interpretations
papers.abstract: Neutrino oscillations successfully describe flavor conversion across a wide range of experiments, yet the origin of several excesses and deficits remains unresolved. This review connects these observations and long-baseline parameter tensions to their proposed physical explanations, clarifying what remains open and how it can be tested. We examine reactor and gallium measurements, accelerator appearance and disappearance searches, and atmospheric constraints, focusing on sterile neutrinos, non-standard interactions, and decoherence in open-system dynamics. For each mechanism, we assess what it modifies, which observations it can address, and which theoretical assumptions and independent constraints limit its viability. Recent results have restricted several interpretations and weakened some earlier tensions; no single extension provides an uncontested account of all observations. We identify the flavor, baseline, energy, and event-topology signatures needed to distinguish competing explanations and assess whether the remaining anomalies require new physics or reflect unresolved flux, interaction, and detector uncertainties.

papers.title: TAN: A Size- and Form-Adaptive Masked-Convolution Encoder for Tissue Graphs
papers.abstract: Tissue graphs represent histology images as graphs over tissue-conforming superpixels, which keeps homogeneous tissue regions intact instead of cutting them into rectangular patches. To embed superpixels, current encoders crop them to bounding boxes and then pad, resize, or mask them, so background or fill values can leak into the node features. This matters in practice, and especially in medical imaging, where a prediction should depend on the tissue and not on an arbitrary preprocessing choice: on BACH, changing only the fill of the masked region shifts the accuracy of frozen encoders by up to 6 percentage points, larger than the differences among the four best encoders under mean fill, and the preferred fill differs between datasets, so it cannot be fixed once and for all. We present TAN (Tissue-Aware Network), a compact convolutional encoder (0.41M parameters) that processes each superpixel at its native shape and extent and excludes background from every operation, which makes its embeddings exactly invariant to the fill by construction. Under identical masks and an identical graph classifier, TAN's accuracy on BACH is not significantly different from that of the 303M-parameter foundation model UNI (81.1% vs. 80.7-82.6%, depending on the fill), with ~740x fewer parameters, ~1,190x fewer FLOPs, and no pretraining. On BRACS, TAN is close to a ResNet18 trained under the same protocol and trails the histopathology foundation models. An ablation with TAN's architecture but standard processing of fill-padded crops shows that masking keeps accuracy similar (nominally higher on BACH, lower on BRACS, within noise) at less than half the FLOPs.

papers.title: Closely spaced change-point detection with an application to geopolitical shocks in oil and gas markets
papers.abstract: Change points that arrive in quick succession, or near the boundaries of the sample, are prone to type-II error: the few observations trapped between successive breaks carry too little information for global procedures to analyze. This article develops a test statistic, $I_1$, for which we derive the limiting null distribution under Gaussian noise, extend the theory to weakly dependent sequences, and prove consistency under a mean-shift alternative. Around $I_1$, we construct DCI, a two-phase algorithm that couples a global scan with multiple local tests via an adaptive-width sliding window. In extensive simulations, $I_1$ and DCI remain Pareto-optimal over criteria spaces spanning true and false positive rates, localization error, and segmentation covering. An application to the US-Iran 2026 conflict quantifies the exposure of energy markets to geopolitical shocks using two new metrics, event sensitivity and event attribution, leading to time series tokenization.

papers.title: Towards optimal selection schedules for online active learning
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of online linear classification, where a stream of unlabeled samples is available, and annotation is costly. We investigate the optimal query policy, that prescribes whether and when a sample should be labeled and used for a training step, or instead discarded, so as to minimize a given objective. We focus on the realizable case, under Gaussian design, in the high-dimensional regime where data dimension and number of unlabeled samples grow proportionally. We consider two objectives: 1) the generalization error under a labeling budget, and 2) a cumulative cost function where mistakes have unit cost and queries cost $Δ$. We first show that the myopic policies that greedily minimize at all times the increment in the objective correspond to either small or intermediate-margin policies, that prescribe the selection of samples whose margins fall within certain intervals that shrink with time. Within this class, we numerically ascertain the optimal schedules for the selection thresholds that minimize the final values of the objectives. Taking inspiration from the myopic policy for the cumulative cost, we design a very simple query policy schedule that we compare to other proposed heuristics, on synthetic data and real medical image datasets. Finally, we discuss myopic policies for two-layer neural networks, and exemplify how naive margin-based policies can cease to be optimal.

papers.title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
papers.abstract: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.

papers.title: HexaShell: A Universal Harness for Robot Coding Agents in Simulation and the Real World
papers.abstract: Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now control robots by writing code, but the strongest of them refine task-specific code over many rounds of trial and revision. Such code tends to overfit the benchmark on which it was tuned, can exploit the benchmark's shortcuts, and is costly to carry over to a new benchmark or robot. We present HexaShell, a thin, task-agnostic harness designed to test how far general tools can go instead. We design a simple and complete set of 14 basic tools, 4 for motion, 5 for perception and 5 for state, which the agent calls in one Python cell per turn. Perception pairs SAM 3, which segments an object from a few words or a click, with NumPy and OpenCV geometry that turns its outlines in several cameras, or a depth image, into its position, size and grasp angle. The API, agent loop and sandbox are shared across all tasks; a new simulator or robot needs only an adapter of 350 to 1,450 lines and a prompt describing its world, and the only task-specific input is an optional skill of about a page of guidance. The same code runs on four simulated benchmarks, built on three simulators with two kinds of arm, and on real robots. With GPT-6-Astra and no task-specific input, HexaShell reaches success rates of 69.9% on RoboDojo, 59.3% on RoboCasa365, 78.3% on LIBERO-PRO and 82.2% on RoboTwin 2.0. With task skills, it reaches 85.0% (score 88.8), 85.6%, 96.7% and 96.8%, respectively, above the best published result we are aware of on each benchmark. The RoboCasa365 result is listed first on its leaderboard. On real dual-arm robots, HexaShell succeeds in 76 of 90 episodes across nine tasks.

papers.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
papers.abstract: Research groups that want a language model grounded in their own literature face a choice between hosted services that receive their unpublished work and self-hosted deployments that keep the data local but give the model no access to the corpus. Munin is an open-source framework for a self-hosted scientific assistant that indexes a group's corpus and its citation graph, and wraps whichever open-weight model the group can serve in an agent harness with specialised reading, search, and computation tools. We claim that the harness, rather than the specific model, is what makes the system useful on domain literature, and we ship the evaluation suite that tests this claim with the software. On 199 paired literature questions, the harness more than doubles the accuracy of the base model, from 0.387 to 0.874 (+0.487, 95% CI [0.407, 0.568]), while naive retrieve-then-answer scores below the unaided model on every backbone tested. Under the harness, roughly twice as many answer claims trace to a passage the model read itself as with fixed top-5 retrieval. When the source paper for a question is removed from the corpus, the system abstains on about nine in ten of the questions it had answered correctly on the Qwen backbones and eight in ten on gpt-oss-20b, and it produces no fabricated local citation across 300 fabricated references. The pattern holds on three backbones from two developers, including a 20-billion-parameter model that runs on a single consumer-grade GPU. With all outbound network access disabled, both Qwen backbones still exceed the published PaperQA2 accuracy. The evaluation suite runs as a single command, so an adopting group can re-run it on its own corpus and model.

papers.title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.

papers.title: On the relation between transformations of SDEs and of associated Kolmogorov equations
papers.abstract: The relationship between transformations of one-dimensional stochastic differential equations and those of the associated Kolmogorov backward equations is investigated. Stochastic transformations combining deterministic time changes, space-time diffeomorphisms, and Girsanov-type changes of probability measure are shown to be in correspondence with admissible transformations of the associated linear parabolic equations, namely the transformations preserving the parabolic structure up to the possible introduction of a zero-order potential term. A distinguished subclass of transformations, characterized by the absence of any potential term in the transformed Kolmogorov equation, is shown to coincide exactly with Doob transformations of the underlying probability measure of the SDE. This characterization further establishes a correspondence between Doob symmetries of an SDE and Lie point symmetries of the associated Kolmogorov backward equation. This correspondence, in turn, yields a constructive (probabilistic) Lie symmetry classification of autonomous Kolmogorov backward equations.

papers.title: Vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy via cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory
papers.abstract: We derive a vibro-polaritonic Raman activity from third-order cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory (CBO-PT) accounting for weak interactions between electrons and low-frequency cavity modes in the vibrational strong coupling (VSC) regime. This work extends the recently presented CBO-PT linear response approach [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2024, 15, 2262-2269] from infrared (IR) to vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy. In a first step, we discuss cavity-induced corrections to the static dipole polarizability tensor, which manifest as molecular and cavity mode contribution determined by the polarization-projected static hyperpolarizability tensor. We then obtain the corresponding vibro-polaritonic Raman activity in double harmonic approximation, which contains molecular, cavity and mixed contributions similar to previously discussed CBO-PT IR intensities. The cavity Raman activity can be interpreted as effective transmission component, which is exclusively determined by the polaritonic Raman response. The methodology and its relation to vibro-polaritonic IR spectroscopy is illustrated for a formaldehyde molecule under VSC. An implementation of the CBO-PT linear response approach for vibro-polaritonic Raman and IR spectroscopies is provided via the open-source Python package CBOvibSpec.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Semi-Lagrangian based bi-fidelity method for the Vlasov--Poisson system with uncertainties
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification for the Vlasov--Poisson (VP) systems entails repeated dynamic simulations, incurring immense computational costs. We develop a structure-preserving Semi-Lagrangian (SL) b-fidelity approximation of macroscopic observables. The MUSCL is used as a low-fidelity solver for pressureless Euler--Poisson system, allowing for a more cost-effective exploration of the stochastic parameter space. A conservative SL scheme combined with high-order discontinuous Galerkin is used as a high-fidelity solver for collisionless VP system, whose mass conservation, positivity preservation, and low numerical dissipation provide a more reliable high-fidelity snapshots for bi-fidelity reconstruction. We further derive a conditional error bound that separates projection, discretization, and model errors. Numerical experiments for both deterministic and uncertain VP problems, including multispecies and higher-dimensional settings, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and robust uncertainty propagation.

papers.title: Lefschetz Pencils on surfaces and an application to Seshadri constants
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We study the question: when does a general pencil in the linear system $|L|$ consist of only irreducible and reduced curves? We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$. The proof is topological, using vanishing cycles and the theory of Lefschetz pencils. As an application, combined with a construction due to Miranda, we prove that for any positive rational number $δ$ there exist a blow up $Y \to X$ at finitely many points, an ample line bundle $M$ on $Y$ and a point $x \in Y$ such that $\varepsilon(Y,M,x) = δ$; Miranda proved this when $X = \mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Near-Extremal Black-Hole Formation Observed from Null Infinity
papers.abstract: We identify near-extremal black-hole formation directly from observables at future null infinity. Fully nonlinear evolutions of the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar system in 3+1 dimensions form black holes with charge-to-mass ratios up to 0.993 from regular, horizon-free, superextremal initial data. Quasinormal frequencies and redshift decay independently recover the near-extremal charge-to-mass ratio. Critical mass scaling is recovered at null infinity and charge scaling at the apparent horizon. The charged scalar Newman--Penrose quantity obeys an asymptotic balance law that replaces the conservation law of the neutral theory.

papers.title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem
papers.abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture asserts that every source-free digraph on $n$ vertices has a quasi-kernel of size at most $n/2$, whereas the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture asks for a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood has size at least $n/2$. Spiro proved that the former implies the latter. In this paper, we establish a weighted transfer theorem: if every nonnegative integer weighting of a source-free digraph $D$ admits a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood contains at least a $θ$-fraction of the total weight, then $D$ has a quasi-kernel of size at most $\lfloor(1-θ)α(D)+θμ\rfloor$ for $0<θ\le1/2$, where $μ$ is the maximum matching size between a maximum independent set and its complement. Using the independent blow-up construction of Spiro, we deduce that the universal small and large quasi-kernel assertions are equivalent for every such $θ$, with no loss in the parameter. In particular, the two conjectures are equivalent. As an application, we prove the half-order bound for source-free break digraphs.

papers.title: On the skew-curvature power law relationship in a stochastic volatility model with infinite variation Lévy jumps
papers.abstract: The short-term blow up behaviour of the ATM-IV skew is commonly modelled by either a rough volatility process with small Hurst index or an infinite variation Lévy process in the log-price dynamics. In this paper, we examine which is the effect of mixed dynamics (i.e. rough volatility and infinite variation Lévy processes) on the ATM-IV skew and curvature. The results of the paper show that the analysis of the leading terms of the short-time expansion of both ATM-IV skew and curvature allow us to determine, from a mixed dynamics model, which mechanism originates the power-law behaviour on the skew and on the curvature. Apart from showing that the mixed model also originates a power law, it has also key implications in model design and calibration. Numerical evidences for the rough Heston model with CGMY Lévy jumps are provided.

papers.title: Stability of Hyperplane Projections of the Regular Simplex and $L_p$-Projection Bodies of balls in $\ell_q^n(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: We prove stability estimates for extremal hyperplane projections of the regular simplex. We further generalize the analogous stability estimates for $\ell_q$-balls by the first named author and the monotonicity theorem for normalized ratios by Barthe and Naor to the $L_p$-setting. To this end, we derive closed formulas for the support functions of their $L_p$-projection bodies, complementing those obtained by the second named author. A key ingredient in our proofs is a stability refinement of the majorization inequality for Gaussian mixtures.

papers.title: Topological Magnetism in 2D and 3D: Skyrmions and Hopfions. Classical and quantum approaches
papers.abstract: We discuss the properties of ferromagnetic skyrmions in relation to the Dzyaloshinskii Moriya interaction, nonlinear sigma models, merons, vortices, frustration, and dipole dipole interactions. Particular attention is given to skyrmion skyrmion interactions and to the dynamical equations governing magnetic textures, including the Landau Lifshitz Gilbert, Thiele, and Landau Lifshitz Bloch equations. The review subsequently extends the discussion to antiferromagnetic systems and to topological structures in three dimensions, with emphasis on Hopfions and their topological characterization. We then examine quantum skyrmions, including approaches that go beyond the semiclassical description, and discuss the emergence of quantum Hopfions. The theoretical framework is complemented by appendices presenting analytical solutions and ansatzes for skyrmions, spin coherent states and path integrals, quantum antiferromagnets, spin torques, fiber-bundle concepts and the Hopf map, and the Euler Lagrange formalism in three dimensions. By connecting continuum field theory, magnetic dynamics, topology, and quantum mechanics, this review aims to provide a coherent framework for understanding the formation, stability, dynamics, interactions, and quantum properties of topological magnetic textures across different dimensions and magnetic systems.

papers.title: Residual Carleman lift for nonlinear lattice Boltzmann simulations
papers.abstract: Low-order Carleman embeddings replace nonlinear dynamics by a larger linear system, but truncation errors can accumulate even when the underlying nonlinear model is accurately approximated by a quadratic equation. We construct a residual Carleman lift (RC2) of lattice Boltzmann dynamics in which an independently evolved spectral background supplies the coefficients and forcing of a second-order residual lift. In a double-shear-layer test, conventional fixed-rest Carleman reaches $87.3\%$ final error, whereas prepared RC2 achieves $0.136\%$ through vortex roll-up, without restarting the lift or using fine-reference feedback. The results demonstrate control of the finite-time accuracy of a fixed-order linear embedding through nonlinear preparation.

papers.title: A Topological Signature of Learning under Noisy Labels
papers.abstract: How does noisy supervision change the representations learned by a neural network? Training accuracy measures agreement with training labels but provides little information about representation geometry. We use persistent homology to track loop structure across distance thresholds in neural activations. Experiments span image classification, text classification, and modular arithmetic. On a fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe, equally sized clean-label and corrupted-label subsets show no detectable persistence difference at epoch 10, whereas corrupted-label subsets have higher persistence at epoch 50. The contrast survives uniform-scale controls, even though predictions match the assigned noisy labels for only 7-11% of corrupted probe examples at that checkpoint. Normalisation preserves the crossover between clean and noisy training trajectories on CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, whereas CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 shows no crossover under any of the five evaluated constructions. In a separate noise-rate calibration comparison across five pipelines, mean activation norm achieves a higher mean in-sample R2 than raw persistence (0.936 versus 0.908). These findings show that noisy supervision leaves a measurable geometric signature even when agreement with corrupted labels is low. Comparing persistence under scale controls with label-fitting measurements offers a way to study how representations respond to label corruption beyond what training accuracy reveals.

papers.title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
papers.abstract: For the biharmonic problem on closed smooth surfaces, we construct a nonconforming finite element method that requires neither stabilization nor the Piola transform. The reduced enriched quartic (REQ) element relies solely on vertex values and scalar edge moments. The same local construction applies to every triangle of a piecewise planar surface. The bilinear form consists of elementwise Laplacian inner products and permits standard finite element assembly. By separating the planar vertex residual from the angle defect contribution, we establish weak discrete Miranda--Talenti-type estimates on both planar meshes and closed piecewise planar surfaces. These estimates guarantee uniform stability on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes. We prove the well-posedness of the method, first-order convergence in the energy norm, and second-order convergence in the broken $H^1$ and $L^2$ norms. Numerical tests on three surfaces show the predicted convergence rates and examine the discrete Miranda--Talenti constants and angle defect scaling.

papers.title: Conservative Numerical Construction of Vlasov-Maxwell Equilibria and an Exact Cancellation of $E\times B$ Flow by an Electrostatic Pressure-Gradient Flow
papers.abstract: A class of Vlasov-Maxwell equilibria with pressure gradients is considered under symmetry assumptions that reduce the equilibrium equations to a nonlinear system of ordinary differential equations. Such equilibria provide self-consistent kinetic states with nonuniform thermodynamic profiles and potentially strong equilibrium electric fields, useful for fully kinetic stability studies of gradient-driven instabilities in the presence of equilibrium flows. The reduced equilibrium problem is posed as a nonlinear boundary-value problem for numerical solution, and a discretization is developed that preserves an associated energy invariant exactly at the discrete level. The resulting method provides a systematic means of computing nontrivial equilibria without relying on scale separation, and an alternative to constructing only approximately self-consistent initial states. A key property of the species flows, identified within this model for any distribution function of the constants of motion, is an exact cancellation between the $E\times B$ flow and an electrostatically generated component of the pressure-gradient-driven flow. This follows directly from a structural property of the species force balance that arises from this type of symmetry reduction, and is verified numerically. Additional numerical results demonstrate the conservative properties of the discretization. Representative equilibrium configurations, relevant to future kinetic instability studies, are also presented. An asymptotic approximation for the interior equilibrium, derived in the well-magnetized, quasi-neutral regime, provides an independent check on these results. The present setting is deliberately simple, providing a controlled framework for constructing and analyzing self-consistent kinetic equilibria and a starting point for extensions to more general symmetry-reduced configurations.

papers.title: Reconnection in 2D Inertial Magnetohydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We consider two-fluid equations of inertial magnetohydrodynamics in two spatial dimensions. These equations can be recast as the evolution of two active scalars, with fluid-like interaction kernels. The equations come in two flavors, left-handed and right-handed. They are conservative and have global unique solutions for both smooth initial data and for initial data in Yudovich class $L^1(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove that the inviscid limit holds in Yudovich class. We prove the persistence of $C^{2,α}$ regularity of patch boundaries through merger events for the left-handed equations. We finally show numerical examples of magnetic reconnection, validating known rigorous results and uncovering new cases.

papers.title: Symmetric two-counter machines
papers.abstract: Counter machines are a particularly simple, Turing-complete model of computation. We study the expressive power of nondeterministic 2-counter machines which are symmetric, in that their set of update transitions is invariant under swapping of counters. Our model is an extension of symmetric 2-VASS, in that we allow modifying both counters within a single transition. As the main result we demonstrate a dramatic impact of symmetry: we show that symmetric 2-counter machines are not Turing-complete, by proving decidability of their reachability problem. We conjecture that the decidability extends to machines with 3 or more counters that are symmetric, meaning the set of update transitions is invariant under any permutation of counters. We leave this problem open for machines with 3 and more counters, while identifying a frontier of the impact of symmetry: we prove undecidability for 3-counter machines invariant under the cyclic permutation group of order 3.

papers.title: FLoTS-SLAM: Optical Flow-Derived Uncertainty for Monocular Dynamic SLAM with Two-Stage Optimization
papers.abstract: Monocular simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) remains challenging in dynamic environments. Real-time dynamic object identification in such environments is a critical problem. Recent approaches estimate per-pixel uncertainty from rendering residuals or multiview feature inconsistency to identify dynamic regions. These methods lack direct motion evidence, and their accuracy may degrade when reconstruction is inaccurate or features are ambiguous. In addition, such uncertainty merely downweights pixels in bundle adjustment (BA), so inaccurate uncertainty estimates can still impair camera pose estimation and 3D reconstruction. Accordingly, we present a monocular RGB SLAM system for dynamic scenes. Specifically, a motion uncertainty estimation method is proposed to derive uncertainty from the residual between optical flow and camera motion induced flow, directly reflecting object motion. The estimation varies with frame alignment accuracy, reducing false detections and yielding accurate pixel-level masks of dynamic regions. To make BA more robust, we estimate camera poses from high confidence pixels. These poses are then used to reproject dynamic pixels during joint refinement of poses and depth, reducing the influence of object motion on both pose and depth updates. Moreover, we provide a quantitative evaluation of dynamic masks and analyze how these masks affect the downstream tracking and reconstruction of dynamic objects. Our approach improves the mean dynamic mask IoU by 35\% over a state-of-the-art baseline on DAVIS, and reduces the average ATE by 59\% on Bonn and 19\% on TUM relative to the SLAM backbone used in our system. The source code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Can coupled thawing quintessence reproduce DESI DR2? A test with two potentials
papers.abstract: DESI DR2 favours dark energy whose equation of state evolves crossing $w=-1$ in the past. Coupled quintessence can produce such an apparent phantom crossing without a phantom field, since a coupled dark sector analysed under the assumption of separate conservation yields an effective equation of state below $-1$. We test whether this mechanism can reproduce the DESI result, using two thawing potentials, a cosine and a double-exponential hilltop, confronted with DESI DR2 BAO, Planck PR4 and three supernova compilations. Both models improve on $Λ$CDM by $Δχ^2 = 5$--$15$, recovering $64$--$92\%$ of the improvement achieved by $w_0w_a$CDM. They track the $w_0w_a$CDM equation of state at $z\lesssim0.4$ but cross the phantom divide later, near $z\simeq1$ rather than $z\simeq0.4$--$0.5$. The coupling is bounded at $|β|<0.073$ ($95\%$), and the two potentials agree on it to within $0.15σ$. They differ instead in the equation of state they can reach: the cosine comes closer to the evolution preferred by DESI and is weakly preferred by the fit. The coupling posterior is bimodal, with modes at $β\simeq\pm0.05$; only the negative mode produces the crossing, and it is the higher of the two in every analysis. In conclusion, the data favour the coupled quintessence phantom crossing but do not yet require it.

papers.title: Unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry in nucleus-nucleus collisions at CERN SPS energies
papers.abstract: The NA61/SHINE experiment at the CERN SPS reports an unexpectedly large excess in the inclusive production of charged over neutral kaons in 0-10% central Ar+Sc collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=8.8$ and 11.9 GeV. This effect corresponds to an unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry, that cannot be explained by known mechanisms contained in the present theoretical models. The comparison of the NA61/SHINE results to data from other experiments reveals, within sizeable uncertainties, a consistent isospin symmetry-violating excess of charged kaon production in the energy regime $2.6<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<200$ GeV. At LHC energies ($0.9<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<13$ TeV) the charged-over-neutral kaon ratio appears consistent with unity, but the uncertainties remain sizeable. A similar excess of charged over neutral kaon yields is observed by NA61/SHINE in minimum bias $π^-$+C reactions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=17.3$ and 25.7 GeV, also in disagreement with model predictions. No clear theoretical explanation of these phenomena has been provided so far. An unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry brings potential heavy consequences for our understanding of particle production, and calls for a concentrated experimental and theoretical effort.
authors: Andrzej Rybicki for the NA61/SHINE Collaboration

papers.title: A Fibre-Integrated SPDC Source of Broadband Polarisation-Entangled Photon Pairs at Telecom Wavelengths using Zn-indiffused PPLN Ridge Waveguides
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs at telecom wavelengths based on a commercially available Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide incorporated within a Sagnac interferometer. Operating across the full degenerate SPDC spectrum using pump-suppression filtering only, the source exhibits a measured bandwidth of approximately 67 nm. Strong non-classical correlations are observed, with an average two-photon interference visibility of 96.9 +/- 0.2 %, a fidelity to the Phi + Bell state of 78.1 %, and a CHSH Bell parameter of S = 2.501 +/- 0.005. We further explore the effect of increasing source brightness on Bell-state performance, revealing the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics in high-flux operating regimes.

papers.title: The Atmospheric Chemistry and Surface Interactions on Mars (ACSIOM) Workshop 2025
papers.abstract: The ACSIOM workshop was held in Cambridge from 10th-12th November 2025. Its primary aims were twofold: 1) to gather UK researchers involved in Mars atmospheric science to identify current shortcomings and challenges in the field, and 2) to discuss possible collaborations and future steps needed to maximise the research output from current and future Mars missions. Workshop attendees spanned a wide range of subjects and disciplines, from atmospheric modellers and surface scientists to experimental chemists and Earth/Venus/exoplanet scientists. One of the primary outcomes of the workshop as identified by the attendees was the need for more collaborations between these different communities. It was agreed that we currently lack sufficient interaction between disciplines and this is a key challenge we need to overcome in order to properly utilise and exploit the vast pool of martian expertise available in the UK. Modellers need reaction rates from experimentalists; experimentalists need modelling context to prioritise their experiments; geologists need modelling context to understand the features they see; modellers need geological context to constrain their results. Attendees stressed that the UK Mars community has a critical mass which is internationally recognised, and improving the communication between communities would allow significant progress to be made in martian research, allowing the UK to maintain leadership in Mars science for years to come. We highlight that this is a pivotal moment for such investments as many planetary missions, both for Mars and other terrestrial bodies, are about to be launched or are being considered in the coming years. Having a strong and close-knit community will be key to better identifying needs and capabilities in order to optimise investments in missions and to have the best scientific return possible.

papers.title: Scaling Spatially Varying Distributed Lag Nonlinear Models for Nationwide Small-Area Data: A Divide-and-Conquer Approach
papers.abstract: Lagged and nonlinear exposure-response relationships are frequently modelled using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs). However, these relationships can vary substantially across locations due to differences in climate, population structure, adaptation and socio-economic characteristics, among others. Spatially-varying DLNMs can capture this heterogeneity, but their computational demands limit their application to fine-scale nationwide datasets with thousands of small areas. In this paper, we adapt a 'divide-and-conquer' approach to spatially varying DLNMs. The method partitions the spatial domain into smaller regions, expands each region with a k-order neighbourhood to reduce boundary effects, fits separate models within each partition using Laplacian P-splines, and combines the resulting estimates using conditional predictive ordinate-based mixture weights. We evaluated the approach in a simulation study based on municipalities in Sicily and applied it to daily summer temperature and mortality data from 7122 municipalities in mainland Italy between 2011 and 2021. Simulation studies show good performance, with relative-risk estimates comparable to those from a global model and relatively robust to the choice and number of partitioning units. Computational efficiency can be substantially improved by using parallel computations. The Italian application reveals significant spatial heterogeneity in the temperature-mortality relationship, with clear regional differences. The proposed framework makes spatially varying DLNMs feasible for large, fine-scale spatiotemporal datasets while retaining location-specific exposure-lag-response estimation.

papers.title: Weak$^*$-weak points of continuity and very smooth points in Bochner function spaces $L^{p}(μ, X)$
papers.abstract: Suppose that $([0,1],\mathcal{A},μ)$ is the Lebesgue measure space and $1< p<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. We prove that an unit vector $h\in L^{p}(μ, X)^*$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(L^{p}(μ, X)^*)$ if and only if $\frac{h(t)}{\|h(t)\|}$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(X^*)$ for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $h(t)\neq 0$, where $X$ is a Banach space such that $X^*$ is separable. As an application of this result, under the same hypothesis on $X$, we prove that a point $f\in L^p(μ, X)_{1}$ is a very smooth point if and only if $\frac{f(t)}{\|f(t)\|}\in S(X)$ is a very smooth point for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $f(t)\neq 0$. We give several examples to show that these results does not hold for $p=1$.

papers.title: HBFSim: A Simulator for Exploring HBF in Memory Hierarchies for LLMs
papers.abstract: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) has recently emerged as a promising technology that provides terabyte-scale accelerator-local capacity at bandwidths approaching HBM, with a potential cost-per-bit advantage over HBM. However, its NAND foundation brings long latency, out-of-place updates, and finite write endurance directly into the accelerator memory hierarchy, making its effects on performance and lifetime difficult to predict. To study this emerging design space, we present HBFSim, an LLM-aware event-driven simulator for heterogeneous HBM+HBF memory systems that preserves application-level memory semantics while modeling flash-internal behavior. HBFSim models HBM, HBF with host-managed flash translation, and conventional capacity tiers in one simulation driven by a calibrated serving frontend. Using HBFSim, we study decoding of Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen3-235B-A22B under three workloads that differ in their input and output lengths. HBF serves data that does not fit in HBM 11.0--19.0$\times$ faster than host DRAM; HBM is better used to hold the running sequences' KV cache than as a cache for HBF; and at a published peak load of Llama-3.1-70B, HBF lasts 2.0 to 6.9 years, in proportion to the stacks that share the KV writes. The artifact is available at https://github.com/FlashLabAE/HBFSim and will track public HBF device data as it becomes available.

papers.title: Weighted spatial averages with missing observations: Convergence and accuracy of delta-method variance approximations
papers.abstract: Weighted spatial averages from incomplete networks are ratios whose variance is approximated by truncating a Taylor series (the delta method). Three questions remain open: whether the series converges, how large a truncation's error is, and how it behaves as the network grows. We address these for observations missing completely at random, independently with a common probability $α$. First, the truncations, which count corrections for the denominator (the total reported weight) and for its coupling with the numerator, converge for a given network only if $α>\tfrac12$ and both corrections increase together. Second, whether or not the series converges, the error of truncations correcting only for the denominator is controlled at any network size by its coefficient of variation $ρ$, with $ρ^2=\tfrac{1-α}α\sum_iβ_i^2$ for weights $β_i$, and by the probability of rare reporting patterns. Third, for uniform weights and bounded fields, these errors vanish as the network grows, at any fixed availability. If correlations also decay with distance, the first-order approximation of earlier work has error of order $ρ^4$, against $ρ^2$ for the simplest approximation. Only truncations of equal order in numerator and denominator, beginning with the first-order truncation, avoid spurious dependence on the mean level; higher ones need not be more accurate. The exact variance for uniform weights, a single sum, shows that for correlated fields the first-order approximation overstates the contribution of missing data but is conservative overall. Concentrated weights degrade it more than $ρ$ indicates. Rainfall simulations over India illustrates results, several of which extend to self-normalized estimators.

papers.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.

papers.title: MLOps-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Production ML Engineering in Real Repositories
papers.abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to modify and maintain machine-learning systems in production, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate either competition-style ML experimentation or generic repository issue resolution. We introduce MLOps-Bench, a repository-grounded benchmark for production ML engineering. Unlike prior ML-agent benchmarks, MLOps-Bench evaluates executable lifecycle changes inside real ML repositories, spanning data pipelines, feature engineering, model training, model serving, monitoring, CI/CD and governance, and end-to-end integration. Each task is grounded in repository evidence and includes a natural-language requirement, oracle patch, plausible buggy baseline, fail-to-pass tests, pass-to-pass tests, and provenance metadata. The benchmark contains 212 validated tasks from 31 public ML repositories, with 636 fail-to-pass tests and 856 pass-to-pass tests. We evaluate six agents and find that the best system solves 31.2% of tasks while passing 68.7% of tests, showing that current agents often make partial progress but still fail production-relevant behavioral requirements. MLOps-Bench shifts agent evaluation beyond model building and issue fixing toward repository-native MLOps work where correctness depends on lifecycle reasoning, behavioral robustness, and preservation of existing system behavior.

papers.title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference enables self-consistent plasma parameter inversion in tokamak integrated data analysis by fusing multi-source diagnostics. However, under nonlinear Gaussian likelihoods, finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate typically relies on sampling methods whose high computational overhead precludes real-time plasma control. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Bayesian inversion framework using a Coherent Ising Machine (CIM)-a quantum computing architecture based on coupled degenerate optical parametric oscillators (DOPOs). With native all-to-all connectivity, the CIM directly maps the negative log-posterior potential onto a spin Hamiltonian and leverages quantum vacuum fluctuations for rapid state-space search during pitchfork bifurcation. Validated on plasma current profile inversion for the EAST tokamak, this method achieves a single-run solution time of approximately 1 ms. Although current qubit limits necessitate a block-wise iterative scheme that prevents full real-time execution today, rapidly scaling quantum hardware offers a clear pathway toward real-time tokamak control.

papers.title: A Note on Carmichael Numbers of the form $ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1)$
papers.abstract: We study integers of the form \[ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1). \] Using Korselt's criterion, we prove that, provided the three factors are prime, $N$ is a Carmichael number if and only if \[ d\equiv4\pmod{12}. \] We also show that the special case $d=2^m$ produces only $1105$ under the prime-factor hypothesis.

papers.title: Adaptive conformal prediction on the Grassmannian
papers.abstract: We introduce a conformal prediction framework for regression with Grassmann-valued responses. The proposed method constructs prediction regions in the form of metric balls directly on the Grassmann manifold, using basis-invariant geometric distances as non-conformity measures and scaling the corresponding non-conformity scores through a learned prediction difficulty estimator. This yields locally adaptive, input-dependent prediction regions that respect the underlying manifold geometry, while retaining the finite-sample marginal coverage guarantee of split conformal prediction under exchangeability. We evaluate several Grassmannian distance metrics and compare their prediction-region efficiency on synthetic benchmarks and an airfoil inverse shape-design problem. The results highlight the advantages of geometry-aware non-conformity scores, while local adaptation improves empirical coverage uniformity across prediction difficulty levels and, in strongly heteroscedastic settings, can substantially reduce prediction-region size while maintaining the target coverage.

papers.title: When Conformal Interfaces Become Logarithmic
papers.abstract: We construct conformal interfaces having defect conformal manifolds between two-dimensional rational CFTs, at least one of which is non-unitary. In a continuous family, interfaces with real and complex spectra can be marginally deformed to each other via their defect moduli parameters. An exceptional point then arises along the trajectory in the conformal manifold, where two interface operators with complex conjugate weights coalesce into a logarithmic pair. We reconstruct the entire trajectory of this novel spectral collision, independently, from self-annulus partition functions and bulk two point correlators in the presence of the interfaces.

papers.title: LSNR: Learned Sparse News Recommendations with Attentive User Modeling
papers.abstract: Current learned sparse approaches for recommender systems, such as STAR, represent a user by concatenating their interaction history into a single query string. For news, this creates two bottlenecks: concatenation collapses a user's distinct reading interests into one flat query, and, because news articles are long-form text, concatenating several news articles quickly overruns the context window of the language model used as backbone and forces quality-degrading truncation. To address both bottlenecks, we introduce learned sparse news recommendations (LSNR). LSNR encodes each article independently and constructs a sparse user vector by combining learned, attention-based weighting of the per-article sparse representations with a dense-projected expansion at the user level. Experiments on the MIND and EBNeRD datasets show that LSNR significantly outperforms STAR, with these gains holding even in short-history settings where truncation is not a factor. Compared to state-of-the-art dense recommenders, LSNR is competitive in standard settings and it outperforms them when the user history is short. An ablation of the user encoder confirms that learned attention-based aggregation outperforms simpler pooling alternatives. Beyond effectiveness, an additional advantage of LSNR is that it serves from an index an order of magnitude smaller than an uncompressed dense baseline.

papers.title: LocalIntent: Outcome-Specific Structured Generation for Backend-Compatible Smart Building Automation with Local LLMs
papers.abstract: Locally deployed large language models (LLMs) can reduce reliance on remote cloud services for natural language smart building automation, but backend-facing processing requires correct outcome selection, alignment with local capabilities, and valid structured outputs. We investigate whether a complete outcome-specific prompting design improves compact-model outputs beyond generic route-then-generate prompting. The proposed LocalIntent approach routes requests to ordinary or persistent-rule branches: the former produces commands, clarifications, or rejections, while the latter generates trigger-action rules, followed by deterministic validation. We evaluate four locally executed Gemma and Qwen models spanning 2B-9B parameters on 101 non-persistent and 54 persistent-rule records, comparing Monolithic prompting, generic two-stage prompting, LocalIntent, and validation-guided repair. Across the evaluated datasets, LocalIntent achieves higher intent understanding, device identification, and action/parameter correctness than generic two-stage prompting, while clarification/mode correctness remains model-dependent. The largest gains occur for rules, where LocalIntent improves intent understanding from 26.4% to 80.6%, device identification from 59.3% to 84.7%, rule-mode correctness from 49.1% to 98.6%, and action/parameter correctness from 5.6% to 44.9%. For non-persistent requests, pooled gains are smaller: intent understanding increases from 39.6% to 53.2%, and action/parameter correctness from 30.7% to 42.8%.

papers.title: topas-editor and TOPilot: tools for AI-driven analysis of diffraction and total scattering data
papers.abstract: This paper describes topas-editor and TOPilot, which provide a powerful interface to the TOPAS software suite and allow generative AI-driven automation of complex crystallographic tasks. topas-editor is a TOPAS-aware VS Code extension designed for the rapid creation and editing of TOPAS input files and for interacting with the software. It knows TOPAS syntax, has crystallographic-aware editing features and provides in-line user guidance via hover tips and automated links to reference manuals. TOPilot is a collection of Python routines and machine-accessible reference documents that allow AI-driven automated analysis in TOPAS. It uses a transferable topas-inp-writer skill that can be applied in all TOPAS application areas. We demonstrate the power and reliability of the approach using examples including: a complex Rietveld refinement with sample- and data-related complications; automatic analysis of multiple data sets; a pipeline from indexing through structure solution to refinement; automatic identification of the phases present in a sample; single crystal and powder diffraction analysis of incommensurate structures; and fitting PDF data. TOPilot can be used directly alongside topas-editor, via a stand-alone topilot-wizard, or via command line interfaces or desktop apps from major AI providers. TOPilot was developed and tested using Claude large language models, but can be configured to use other cloud or local models. topas-editor and TOPilot are freely available.

papers.title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

papers.title: Timelike entanglement entropy with gravitational anomaly from complexified geometry
papers.abstract: We investigate the timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) in a two-dimensional conformal field theory with a gravitational anomaly, $c_L\neq c_R$, dual to topologically massive gravity in AdS$_3$. Holographically, the TEE is determined by the on-shell action of a massive spinning particle on a single complex geodesic anchored at the endpoints of the timelike interval. This action consists of the complex geodesic length and the twist of a parallel-transported normal frame. We carry out the computation in Poincaré AdS$_3$, non-extremal and extremal rotating BTZ backgrounds, and provide an equivalent Chern-Simons derivation in which the bulk connection stays real while only the saddle of the Wilson-line probe becomes complex. In each case, the holographic result matches the corresponding TEE in dual field theory. The real part of the TEE is fixed unambiguously whereas its imaginary part depends on the boundary $iε$ prescription and the orientation of the interval. In the bulk, the dependence on orientation reflects an ambiguity in the choice of framing. Along the complex geodesic, the residual frame group becomes $SO(2,\mathbb C)\simeq\mathbb C^*$, so the endpoint conditions determine the frame twist only up to integer multiples of $2πi$. The difference between the two orientations, $\frac{c_L-c_R}{6}\,iπ$, is fixed entirely by the gravitational anomaly and persists for the Rényi pseudo-entropies.

papers.title: Dihedral fields with Bloch lattice index five and quadratic subfield Q(i)
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many Galois extensions $M/\mathbb{Q}$ with dihedral group of order ten, quadratic subfield $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and Bloch lattice index $Q_2(M)=5$. More precisely, we specify a Chebotarev set of rational primes of density $1/50$. For every prime $\ell$ in this set, at least two of four mixed cyclic quintic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ of conductor $(25\ell)$ have this index and satisfy $K_2(O_M)(5)\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/5)^2$. A two-dimensional cup-product pencil selects the extensions. Generalized Bockstein maps, integral co-descent, and a motivic genus formula then determine the tame kernel and the subfield Bloch-lattice index. The result is unconditional.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware AI-enabled framework for predicting hydrogen dispersion in confined spaces to enhance operator situational awareness
papers.abstract: We present a two-stage AI-enabled framework for enhancing operator situational awareness during compressed hydrogen bunkering in maritime confined spaces. In the event of a leak, the framework first estimates the unknown leakage rate from early sensor readings and then forecasts how the hydrogen cloud will disperse over the next time steps, providing operators with a predicted concentration map together with confidence bounds. The framework is based on two independent AI models building one AI system. The AI system is designed as a decision-support tool. It augments sensor readings, and thus enhances operator situational awareness and supports decision-making. This enables preventive safety barriers to be deployed before hazardous concentrations are reached, while an independent emergency shutdown system remains the ultimate safety layer. The system design incorporates safeguards to ensure the AI system operates within its competence envelope. Trained and tested on an open dataset of confined-space hydrogen releases, the framework achieves a mean absolute error of $0.052$~g/s in leakage-rate estimation and $\approx0.018$ in hydrogen-concentration prediction, approaching the sensor precision bound of $\pm0.01$. The hydrogen-concentration prediction provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates that allow operators to judge the reliability of each forecast. These results suggest that the framework may provide early information about hazardous concentration build-up, potentially supporting preventive actions by operators.

papers.title: On the crystalline Artin--Mumford invariant
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $W=W(k)$. We prove that the torsion subgroup of $H^3_{\mathrm{cris}}(X/W)$ is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties over $k$. The proof combines the action of correspondences on Hodge--Witt cohomology and on the first Nygaard piece of the de Rham--Witt complex.

papers.title: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
papers.abstract: We develop a framework to identify and quantify arbitrage across logically related prediction-market contracts. We prove that prices outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors admit arbitrage and identify optimal arbitrage portfolios through integer programming.
